live_assumptions.statement: When a live no-fault continuity claim collides with reserve depletion, host-capacity shortage, or cross-node responsibility denial, the archive should escalate from ordinary reserve handling to a temporary stronger floor rather than letting support collapse on a raw first-come-first-served basis: pause adverse clocks, keep the baseline non-learner-borne, route urgent cases by narrow continuity-risk facts, and use a named shared override when local capacity or authority cannot restore the floor in time.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after a reserve or entitlement posture has already been published but real scarcity or capacity limits emerge while the continuity window is still live.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows ordinary first-come-first-served reserve handling usually protects learners as well as or better than a temporary stronger-floor rule, so the archive materially overstates the need for anti-race escalation.

Evidence shows reserve depletion or host-capacity shortages usually cannot be managed through clock-stops, provisional holds, or shared overrides without creating larger unfairness or unusable false promises, so the archive materially overstates what can travel as a scarcity floor.

Evidence shows the narrow continuity-risk facts used here do not meaningfully outperform richer discretionary hardship review or local queue design, so the archive overstates the portability of a small anti-race priority layer.

live_assumptions.statement: When a temporary stronger no-fault continuity floor is itself oversubscribed, only a very small scarcity grammar should travel across sectors: sort first by near-term route-loss facts (`PF1-PF4`), batch by disruption cohort or short hold windows rather than click-speed (`SB1-SB3`), publish a thin learner-facing scarcity layer (`SF1-SF7`), and treat repeated use of the same stronger-floor override as evidence that the route should harden into reserve, entitlement, or predeclared capacity design rather than rerun emergency triage indefinitely.

live_assumptions.statement: When the same route repeatedly reaches stronger-floor scarcity (`ES2` / `ES3`), the archive should graduate from pure emergency triage into the smallest truthful predeclared capacity posture: `CP1` multi-destination planning when destination rediscovery is the recurring problem, `CP2` shadow-capacity when a small protected margin is the real bottleneck, and `CP3` shared-slot pooling when continuity already depends on several nodes rather than one host alone; that layer should travel only through a thin cross-node packet (`XC1-XC7`) rather than full partner-contract portability.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity has shown that emergency stronger-floor handling is recurring on the same route family and some predeclared continuity-capacity design may now be owed before the next disruption.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows repeated stronger-floor scarcity is usually best handled by renewed emergency override rather than any reusable predeclared capacity posture, so the archive materially overstates the need for `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` hardening.

Evidence shows exact seat counts, partner-contract terms, or detailed allocation formulas must usually travel with predeclared continuity planning for it to be truthful, so the archive materially understates how much of the capacity layer must be portable.

Evidence shows multi-destination maps, shadow margins, and shared-slot pools do not track the real cross-sector bottlenecks that cause repeated continuity scarcity, so the archive overstates the value of this small `CP0-CP3` grammar.

live_assumptions.statement: Once repeated stronger-floor scarcity has hardened into `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning, the archive should publish only a very small learner-visible shell (`LV1-LV8`) plus a tiny freshness grammar (`FS0-FS2`, `RA1-RA3`): learners should be able to see route scope, protected cohort, posture type, continuity promise, activation owner, destination shape, freshness state, and fallback path, while exact counts, contracts, and settlement mechanics remain partner-facing; stale arrangements may remain partner-side leads but should not continue as live learner-facing continuity promises after they lapse.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity has already been hardened into some predeclared continuity-capacity posture.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows learners usually need exact seat counts, named-host guarantees, or full contract terms for predeclared continuity planning to remain truthful, so the archive materially understates what must become learner-visible.

Evidence shows partner-side confidentiality or host volatility usually prevents even a thin `LV1-LV8` shell from remaining current enough to publish honestly, so the archive materially overstates what continuity planning can say publicly before activation.

live_assumptions.statement: Once `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` continuity planning is learner-visible, the archive should separate hidden partner maintenance from learner-facing republication with a very small materiality ladder (`MC0-MC3`) and should allow lapsed routes to remain learner-visible only through a still smaller provisional-lead ladder (`PL0-PL2`): visible route, location, delivery, approval, price-floor, cohort, or activation-owner changes that matter for informed learner reliance should force republication or downgrade, while only narrow timing/capacity uncertainty may keep the same named destination visible as an `FS1` verify-on-activation lead.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity has already hardened into learner-visible `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning.

live_assumptions.statement: Once learner-visible `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` continuity planning sits in `FS1` or provisional states, the archive should separate route-detail publication into a tiny `DD0-DD3` ladder: keep a named destination only where the same receiving host/path still stands and unresolved uncertainty is narrow timing or capacity confirmation; publish only a destination family where the route class still stands but the specific host/path does not; publish only an owner-contact shell where even a family statement would overstate what is live; and keep route detail fully off-shell where only partner memory remains. Sector and posture should matter: higher-ed `CP2` routes can usually carry more `DD3` than pooled `CP3` routes, workforce/library continuity often cools first to `DD2` or `DD1`, and professional/practicum routes usually cool to `DD1` / `DD2` until activation because host and licensure facts move quickly.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity has already hardened into learner-visible `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning and the route has fallen into `FS1` or another provisional-lead state.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows learners usually need named destinations to remain public even when approval, location, host, or charge-floor certainty is no longer narrow, so the archive materially overstates the need to downgrade from `DD3` to `DD2` / `DD1` once those facts move.

live_assumptions.statement: Once learner-visible `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning has already cooled to activated `DD1` or `DD2` shells, those shells should resolve within a small visible clock into one of only three honest outputs: `AR1` named destination where one host/path is genuinely ready, `AR2` equivalent-option set where several materially comparable routes already preserve the continuity floor, or `AR3` explicit no-route-yet notice where neither is yet truthful. live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity has already hardened into learner-visible `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning and a learner has actually activated a `DD1` or `DD2` shell.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows activated provisional shells can usually remain truthful for long periods without a bounded learner-facing route-resolution clock, so the archive materially overstates the need for `AK1-AK3` / `RK1-RK3` discipline.

Evidence shows workforce, higher-ed, or practicum continuity routes usually need richer or different learner-facing activated outputs than `AR1` / `AR2` / `AR3`, so the archive materially understates what must be published after activation begins.

Evidence shows bounded equivalent-option sets are rarely real and that activated continuity should almost always jump straight from provisional shell either to a named route or to full no-route failure, so the archive materially overstates the value of `AR2`.

live_assumptions.statement: Once activated continuity publication has reached a genuine multi-route `AR2` state, the archive should make equivalence inspectable through a very small `EQ1-EQ6` field set covering recognition, learner charges, timing, delivery/access, approval status, and support/handoff burden; should reject `AR2` wherever any option creates material recognition, cost, delivery, or approval drift (`MV1-MV4`) not neutralized by the same no-fault floor; and should allow defaulting only as a reversible protection-preserving hold (`CH2`) rather than as a sticky or under-supported assignment that quietly pushes the learner onto a worse route.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity has already hardened into learner-visible `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning and a learner has actually been given a live multi-route `AR2` option set.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows materially comparable activated route sets usually require a much richer or sector-specific field list than `EQ1-EQ6`, so the archive materially understates what a learner must see before an `AR2` choice is truthful.

Evidence shows silent or lightly supported default assignment usually remains continuity-preserving even when switching is costly, slower, or loss-bearing, so the archive materially overstates the need for reversible no-loss switching as a condition of truthful `CH2` handling.

live_assumptions.statement: Once a genuine `AR2` equivalent-option set already exists, the archive should allow only a very small first-assignment layer: `FA1` neutral pre-hold, `FA2` explained soft recommendation, and `FA3` protective temporary default may remain truthful only while the learner receives `XF1-XF5`, keeps `SW1-SW5`, and gets at least the applicable `HD1-HD3` switch window after clear notice; once those no-loss protections fall away, the state is no longer honestly `AR2` and should be restated as `AR1`, rebuilt, or individualized.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after a learner has already reached a genuine multi-route `AR2` continuity state and first assignment or routing help is about to occur.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows first-assignment handling inside truthful multi-route continuity almost always needs a much richer or more sector-specific grammar than `FA1-FA4`, `HD1-HD3`, `XF1-XF5`, and `SW1-SW5`, so the archive materially understates what must be published and preserved once routing help begins.

Evidence shows a route may usually remain honest `AR2` even when switching after first assignment loses queue position, payer protection, proof carryover, or review ownership, so the archive materially overstates the need for `SW1-SW5` no-loss carryover.

Evidence shows temporary recommendation or default practices usually remain fair even without a clear individualized explanation or usable post-notice switch window, so the archive materially overstates the need for `XF1-XF5` and `HD1-HD3` discipline.

live_assumptions.statement: Once a genuine `AR2` continuity set has moved through first assignment, the archive should let `SW1-SW5` narrow only through a small switch-taper grammar: weak admin-only movement (`CF1`) is never enough; strong route-consumption facts (`CF2-CF5`) may justify only prospective, component-specific taper (`TP2`) or ordinary-route conversion (`TP3`); and already absorbed continuity costs, proof/record carryover, and review ownership should not be erased merely because one route began consuming support, aid handling, attendance time, or host preparation.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after a learner has already reached a genuine multi-route `AR2` continuity state and the system is deciding whether post-assignment switch rights should continue, taper, or convert into ordinary local route rules.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows post-assignment switch rights usually need a much richer or more sector-specific taper grammar than `TP0-TP3` and `CF1-CF5`, so the archive materially understates what has to be published or preserved once a route begins to consume real resources.

Evidence shows weak administrative movement such as estimated aid packaging, ordinary onboarding, or record sync is usually enough to justify narrowing no-loss switch rights, so the archive materially overstates the distinction between `CF1` and strong route-consumption facts.

Evidence shows actual support spend, aid disbursement, attendance, or host preparation usually permits retroactive billing, loss of record/proof carryover, or reset of review ownership, so the archive materially overstates the need for prospective-only taper and surviving accountability protections.

live_assumptions.statement: Once a genuine `AR2` continuity set has already moved into `TP2` or `TP3`, earlier taper should not be treated as permanent closure of no-fault protection: if post-start route deterioration later occurs through a small set of system-caused facts (`DF1-DF5`) — timing/delivery drift, recognition/approval drift, capacity or host-performance failure, charge/aid/support deterioration, or route closure / legal shutoff — the archive should reopen continuity through a small `RO0-RO3` grammar rather than laundering the new disruption into ordinary learner-progress risk.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after a learner has already started on or been converted into a `TP2` / `TP3` route and the destination later worsens, changes, or fails.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows post-start route deterioration usually needs a much richer or more sector-specific reopen grammar than `RO0-RO3` and `DF1-DF5`, so the archive materially understates what must happen once a started route later worsens.

Evidence shows route-side timing, approval, partner, support, or closure failures after start usually should still be treated as ordinary learner-progress risk rather than as fresh continuity events, so the archive materially overstates the need for reopen-after-taper handling.

Evidence shows earlier taper or ordinary-route conversion usually eliminates payer protection, proof/record carryover, or accountability ownership even when the assigned route later fails for system-caused reasons, so the archive materially overstates the need for continuity reopening after post-start deterioration.

live_assumptions.statement: Once post-start route deterioration has truthfully reopened continuity under `RO2` or `RO3`, the archive should restore earlier protection through a small revival ladder (`RB0-RB3`): ordinary `RO2` cases usually revive only the impaired components of priority, scarcity, payer, and portability, ordinary `RO3` cases usually revive the fuller continuity stack, and where exact old slots or destinations cannot literally return the system still owes the nearest truthful equivalent protected band rather than back-of-line restart, retro-billing, or restart-from-zero packet demands.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after a learner has already moved into `TP2` / `TP3`, the route later deteriorates through `DF1-DF5`, and continuity has truthfully reopened under `RO2` or `RO3`.
invalidation_triggers: Evidence shows reopened continuity usually needs a much richer or more sector-specific revival grammar than `RB0-RB3`, so the archive materially understates what must return once a started route later fails.

Evidence shows learners whose assigned destination later fails are usually not owed restored queue seniority, same-or-better scarcity treatment, or equivalent protected-band rebuilding, so the archive materially overstates the need for `RB1-RB3` revival rather than ordinary re-entry.

Evidence shows failed-route residue, partial support spend, or real consumption usually permits back-of-line restart, retro-billing, or restart-from-zero packet demands even when the destination later fails for system-caused reasons, so the archive materially overstates the survival of no-fault waivers, offsets, and packet carryover after reopen.

live_assumptions.statement: Once continuity has truthfully reopened and revived protection under `RB1-RB3`, failed-route residue may stay inside offset / waiver treatment only while the learner still has a reasonable opportunity to complete on the protected terms and no live nonportable loss, material support / maintenance loss, or legally sticky debt state remains unneutralized; once those conditions fail, the archive should escalate through a small residue ladder (`ER0-ER3`) to refund, compensation, formal continuity-failure notice, or debt-relief / discharge guidance rather than treating internal credits as a complete remedy.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after a learner has already moved into `TP2` / `TP3`, the route later deteriorates through `DF1-DF5`, continuity has truthfully reopened under `RO2` / `RO3`, and revival under `RB1-RB3` has already been assessed.

live_assumptions.statement: Once failed-route residue has truthfully escalated into `ER1`, `ER2`, or `ER3`, the archive should require one thin escalation packet rather than a single preferred remedy offer: a small learner-facing notice shell (`NS1-NS8`), a minimum evidence packet (`EV1-EV6`), named owner roles (`OW1-OW3`), timing / refresh defaults (`TM1-TM3`), and a non-waiver rule (`NW1-NW4`) so accepting one internal remedy does not silently erase still-live complaint, regulator, refund, compensation, or discharge routes except for later reconciliation of duplicate monetary recovery.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, transfer / teach-out situations, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum continuity routes after `ER1-ER3` escalation is already truthful because failed-route residue can no longer be fully absorbed inside offset / waiver treatment alone.

live_assumptions.statement: Once `ER1-ER3` escalation is truthful, the archive should allow one shared cohort-core packet only for facts that are genuinely common, should require subgroup or learner-specific supplements as soon as route, money, support, timing, or external-rights facts materially diverge (`CG0-CG3`, `IS1-IS5`), and should require refresh when route status, money status, owner / clock status, or external-rights relevance materially changes after the first notice (`RF1-RF5`).

live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, teach-out / transfer continuity, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum routes once failed-route residue has already escalated into `ER1-ER3` and a learner-facing escalation packet is already required.

live_assumptions.statement: Once an `ER1-ER3` escalation packet truthfully marks unresolved route, money, and external-rights fields with `UF0-UF4`, `MK1-MK6`, and `GU1-GU4`, learner action should split into a small portable posture ladder (`PA0-PA4`) and matching pause / restart rules (`PC0-PC4`): provisional packets may support browsing, comparison, and reversible holds, but materially ambiguous route / money / rights fields should not drive binding election, transfer, acceptance, settlement, waiver, or adverse clock loss until refreshed notice narrows the ambiguity enough for a truthful final decision.
live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, teach-out / transfer continuity, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum routes once failed-route residue has already escalated into `ER1-ER3` and a learner-facing escalation packet is already required.

live_assumptions.scope: Public-route AI-learning transitions, teach-out / transfer continuity, workforce and library continuity supports, and professional / practicum routes once an `ER1-ER3` escalation packet has already paused a route, money, or external-rights clock under `PC1-PC4` and ambiguity later narrows enough for that clock to restart.
